Following the discussion at the board meeting back in February, as Jen referenced, one thing was clear. Housing is a complex issue that requires a thoughtful and coordinated communication approach. But first, I'll provide a brief overview of the communication strategy designed to help build understanding,

elevate awareness, and support ongoing engagement around this work. We know that solving a challenge of this scale requires a common message supported by many voices. With this strategy, we'll address that. At its core, this effort is about people, not buildings. Housing affects young families, older adults, workers, small businesses, employers, and long-time residents alike. The framework communicates the fact that housing issues impact everyone in our

community and the solutions will require a county-wide effort. The proposed tagline, Housing solutions for every neighbor across Fairfax County is intended to reinforce three ideas. First, that housing solutions will require innovation, creativity, and a range of tools and approaches. Second, that housing needs vary across households and stages of life. And third, that this is a county-wide issue affecting every community member in Fairfax County. The secondary message, breaking down barriers and building homes to keep our local economy strong and growing,

reflects the broader work underway. Breaking down barriers speaks to the efficiencies and process improvements necessary to reach our goal. Building homes recognize the need to increase housing supply and address a housing production shortfall. And as you heard earlier today, housing and economic development are interconnected, which is why we are also emphasizing the broader economic benefits of this work. Under this messaging strategy, we have four focus areas. Each highlights a different aspect of the work underway to make Fairfax County a place where everyone can live,

work, and thrive. First, production. Fairfax County must produce more housing to keep pace with the needs of our growing and diverse workforce. Second, solutions. Developing housing solutions is a priority for the Board of Supervisors, as highlighted earlier today by Ben in the task force report. Third, affordability. Housing pressures affect many residents, but those at the lower end of the spectrum are often impacted the most.

As you know, even households earning a solid income can face housing affordability challenges. Finally, the benefits. Developing housing solutions uplifts the entire community, taxpayers, homeowners, small businesses, and families alike.

These messages are intended to be flexible and adapted depending on the audience, platform, or story. For example, within your individual districts, some messaging may resonate more with young families, while others may be more relevant to retirees or older adults.

the intent is to provide a common framework that can be adapted to fit the needs of your district or your community. So how do we bring all these messages to life? assets, video, and other materials to help reinforce common messaging. From there, we can distribute this content across county platforms and partner channels to reach key audiences.
